data.name: Tripurari
data.gender_notes: Tripurari is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The ruler of the three cities of the cosmos, Tripura. Tripura refers to the three cities of Maya, Vibhava, and Tripura, which are the three aspects of the god Shiva. The name Tripurari carries the meaning “Three-City-Ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Bengali. Parents who choose Tripurari usually hope their child will grow to embody three-city-ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine power of Shiva and his role as the ruler of the universe.
data.etymology: Tripurari belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Three-City-Ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tripurari total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Rama, an iconic figure in Hinduism, is famous for his righteousness, courage, wisdom, and dedication to honor and dharma. His epic story, the Ramayana, continues to be one of the most widely read texts in Indian literature, and Rama's portrait as an ideal king, husband, and hero has influenced countless artists, literary works, and cultural traditions across India.
data.spiritual_significance: Rama represents the divine qualities of truth, peace, love, and duty. He is often seen as an embodiment of purity, selflessness, and righteousness. The journey of Rama in his various avatars, including his exile, the battle against the demon king Ravana, and his ultimate return to his kingdom, illustrates the importance of devotion, detachment, and perseverance in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tripurari is a name for the divine form of Shiva, the destroyer of three cities (Tripura) representing ignorance, attachment, and ego. It symbolizes the triumph of divine consciousness over the destructive influences of material desire.
